title: `torch.load()` without `weights_only=True` — arbitrary code execution risk
description: Five `torch.load()` calls across `model_manager.py:221,300`, `model_versioning.py:594`, `artifact_manager.py:180`, `training/evaluate_models.py:91` omit `weights_only=True`. PyTorch 2.0+ warns this allows arbitrary pickle execution when loading untrusted `.pth` files.
recommendation: Add `weights_only=True` to all `torch.load()` calls. For full model objects use `torch.serialization.add_safe_globals()` pattern.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "torch.load" backend/ml/ | grep -v weights_only` returns no results

title: XGBoost model R²=−0.011, all feature importances zero
description: `evaluation_report.json` reports R²=−0.011 (worse than predicting the mean) and direction_accuracy=46.5% (below coin flip). `xgboost_training_results.json` shows all 57 feature importances as 0.0 — the model learned nothing. This suggests a data pipeline bug (e.g., target leakage, improper scaling, or empty training split).
recommendation: Audit training data pipeline: verify target variable construction, check train/test split for look-ahead bias, ensure feature values are non-zero before training. Add assertion `r2 > 0.0` as model acceptance gate.
acceptance_test_hint: `python -m backend.ml.training.evaluate_models` reports `r2 > 0.0` and at least one non-zero feature importance

title: Path traversal in model name parameter — arbitrary file load
description: `load_model(model_name)` constructs `Path(f"backend/ml_models/{model_name}.pkl")` with no validation. An attacker can pass `model_name="../../../etc/passwd"` via `POST /models/../../../etc/passwd/load` to attempt loading arbitrary files via joblib, or enumerate paths.
recommendation: Validate `model_name` against `re.fullmatch(r"[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", model_name)` before path construction. Use `Path.resolve()` and assert the resolved path is within `models_path`.
acceptance_test_hint: `curl -X POST http://localhost:8001/models/../../../etc/passwd/load` returns 400, not 500

title: Hardcoded relative path in FileHandler — fails when CWD is not project root
description: `logging.FileHandler(f'backend/ml_logs/training_{...}.log')` uses a relative path. When the script is run from any directory other than the project root (e.g., from `/app` in Docker or from `backend/`), the log directory will not be found and training will fail silently or crash. `simple_training_pipeline.py:26` has the same issue.
recommendation: Replace relative path with `Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "ml_logs" / f"training_{...}.log"` or use `os.getenv("ML_LOGS_PATH")`.
acceptance_test_hint: Training pipeline runs from any working directory and produces log files at the correct absolute path

title: Feature store builtin coverage is much narrower than documented
description: Documentation (`ML_PIPELINE_DOCUMENTATION.md`) claims the feature store manages "MACD, Bollinger Bands, sentiment features, volatility, volume patterns, correlation metrics." The `builtin_features` dict at `feature_store.py:341-353` only implements: `price_return_1d`, `price_return_5d`, `price_volatility_20d`, `volume_ratio_20d`, `rsi_14d`, `sma_20d`, `ema_20d`, `pe_ratio`, `market_cap` (9 features). MACD, Bollinger Bands, and sentiment are absent.
recommendation: Implement missing technical indicators or update documentation to reflect actual scope. Add `_compute_macd()`, `_compute_bollinger_bands()` methods and register them.
acceptance_test_hint: Feature store `builtin_features` dict contains at minimum MACD and Bollinger Band compute functions

title: Hardcoded developer absolute path for `data_dir`
description: `"data_dir": "/Users/yluo/Documents/Code/ScAI/FR1-data"` is a personal machine path. Any deployment other than the original developer's laptop will silently produce empty results or raise `FileNotFoundError` on all offline data tools.
recommendation: Replace with `os.getenv("TRADINGAGENTS_DATA_DIR", str(Path.home() / "tradingagents-data"))` or a project-relative fallback; document env var in README.
acceptance_test_hint: `assert os.path.isabs(DEFAULT_CONFIG["data_dir"])` passes and path is derived from env var in a fresh env without that filesystem path.

title: `fundamentals_report` variable assigned `news_report` value
description: Line 14: `fundamentals_report = state["news_report"]` — the fundamentals report is never read; instead the news report is passed twice into the LLM context string on line 18. The Risk Manager therefore cannot reason about fundamentals data at all.
recommendation: Change line 14 to `fundamentals_report = state["fundamentals_report"]`.
acceptance_test_hint: Unit test: construct a state where `news_report != fundamentals_report`, invoke `risk_manager_node`, assert the prompt contains `fundamentals_report` content not duplicated `news_report`.

title: File handle leak in `get_data_in_range`
description: `data = open(data_path, "r")` is never closed. In a backtest loop over many dates/tickers this will exhaust the OS file descriptor limit and raise `OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files`.
recommendation: Replace with `with open(data_path, "r") as f: data = json.load(f)` and remove the separate `json.load(data)` call.
acceptance_test_hint: Pytest with `mock_open` verifies `__exit__` is called; OS-level FD count does not grow during a 100-iteration loop.

title: `FinancialSituationMemory` uses OpenAI client for embeddings regardless of provider
description: The constructor creates `self.client = OpenAI(base_url=config["backend_url"])` and always calls `client.embeddings.create`. For Anthropic or Google providers the base URL is incompatible; the embedding call will fail with an HTTP error, causing `reflect_and_remember` to raise at runtime.
recommendation: Gate embedding client on provider: use OpenAI client only for OpenAI/Ollama/OpenRouter; skip embeddings or raise a clear `NotImplementedError` for unsupported providers. Long-term, use `langchain_community` embeddings that match the provider.
acceptance_test_hint: Integration test with `llm_provider="anthropic"` config does not crash on `reflect_and_remember`.

title: OpenAI `responses.create` API call stores conversation data server-side (`store=True`)
description: `get_stock_news_openai`, `get_global_news_openai`, and `get_fundamentals_openai` all pass `store=True` to `client.responses.create`. This persists potentially sensitive ticker/date queries in OpenAI's servers, which may violate data residency or compliance requirements for a financial platform.
recommendation: Set `store=False` unless explicit user opt-in; add a config key `openai_store_responses` defaulting to `False`.
acceptance_test_hint: Config-driven test asserts `store` kwarg value matches config setting.

title: LLM provider branch uses `ChatOpenAI` for Ollama/OpenRouter without appropriate headers
description: The `ollama` and `openrouter` providers are handled via `ChatOpenAI` pointing at a custom `backend_url`, but OpenRouter requires `x-title` and `HTTP-Referer` headers that `ChatOpenAI` does not add by default. Ollama may need `num_ctx` model param. Silent degradation or auth errors will occur at runtime.
recommendation: Add provider-specific configuration: for OpenRouter pass `default_headers` to `ChatOpenAI`; for Ollama pass `model_kwargs`. Add a `"openrouter"` explicit branch or document limitations.
acceptance_test_hint: CLI integration test with mocked OpenRouter endpoint asserts required headers are present.

title: Wildcard `from tradingagents.agents import *` used in critical graph wiring
description: `setup.py:8`, `trading_graph.py:15`, `agent_states.py:5` all use `from tradingagents.agents import *`. This makes the import surface implicit, prevents static analysis tools from resolving names, and means any future accidental `__all__` change breaks graph compilation silently.
recommendation: Replace star imports with explicit imports of the symbols actually used (`create_market_analyst`, `GraphSetup`, etc.).
acceptance_test_hint: `mypy --strict` on `graph/setup.py` reports no "Name not defined" errors.

title: `trader_node` signature takes `name` as positional but `functools.partial` passes it as keyword
description: `trader_node(state, name)` is called via `functools.partial(trader_node, name="Trader")`. LangGraph calls nodes with a single positional argument `(state,)`. The partial wrapping means `name` will never be passed correctly by LangGraph's node invocation, so `name` will always be the partial-captured `"Trader"` string — which is the intended behavior, but the function signature is misleading and fragile. Additionally, `sender` is set in the return dict but not declared in `AgentState`.
recommendation: Refactor to a closure like the other agent factories; remove the `functools.partial` pattern. Declare `sender` in `AgentState` or remove the key from the return dict.
acceptance_test_hint: `AgentState.__annotations__` contains `sender`; mypy passes on trader.py.

title: `setup.py` pins stale/missing package versions; no `langchain-anthropic` or `langchain-google-genai`
description: `setup.py` installs `langchain-openai>=0.0.2` (current is `>=0.1`) and lists `langchain>=0.1.0` but does NOT include `langchain-anthropic` or `langchain-google-genai`, which are imported unconditionally in `trading_graph.py:11-12`. Installing via `pip install tradingagents` and using Anthropic/Google providers will fail with `ImportError`.
recommendation: Add `langchain-anthropic>=0.1.0` and `langchain-google-genai>=1.0.0` to `install_requires`; pin `langchain-openai>=0.1.0`.
acceptance_test_hint: Fresh virtualenv install; `python -c "from tradingagents.graph.trading_graph import TradingAgentsGraph"` succeeds without extra manual installs.

title: Unconditional selenium import breaks entire ETL package
description: `from selenium import webdriver` at module top-level; no try/except guard. `backend/etl/__init__.py` re-exports `DataExtractor` which imports through this chain. Entire `backend.etl` package fails to import, making ETL, orchestrator, and all callers non-functional. Confirmed: `python3 -c "from backend.etl.data_extractor import DataExtractor"` → `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'selenium'`
recommendation: Wrap selenium imports in try/except with `SELENIUM_AVAILABLE = False` fallback, identical to how `talib`/`torch` are handled in other modules. Only the Selenium-specific scraping path should fail gracefully.
acceptance_test_hint: `python3 -c "from backend.etl.data_extractor import DataExtractor; print('OK')"` exits 0

title: Infinite loop when distributed jobs do not complete normally
description: `while completed_jobs < len(job_ids)` at line 152 only increments when jobs reach `status == "completed"`. If jobs stall in "running", "failed", or "error" status (e.g., due to exception in processor worker), the loop never exits. No timeout, no break on failed-job accumulation. `processing_task` is also never awaited or cancelled on loop exit.
recommendation: Add loop timeout (e.g., `max_wait_seconds = config.job_timeout_hours * 3600`), count failed+completed toward exit condition, cancel `processing_task` in finally block.
acceptance_test_hint: Integration test: mock all jobs to fail; assert orchestrator returns within 60s

title: SmartDataFetcher is entirely stub — returns mock zeros for all data types
description: Every fetch method (`_fetch_price_data`, `_fetch_fundamentals`, `_fetch_news`, `_fetch_financials`, `_fetch_earnings`, `_fetch_sentiment`, `_fetch_generic`) returns hardcoded `{"source": "mock", "price": 0.0, ...}`. Any component consuming this receives fabricated data silently. The module docstring claims "intelligent caching and rate limit management."
recommendation: Implement real fetch logic by delegating to the existing `FinnhubClient`, `AlphaVantageClient`, `SECEdgarClient`, `PolygonClient` in `data_ingestion/`. Wire cache_manager and rate_limiter parameters.
acceptance_test_hint: Unit test: `fetcher.fetch_stock_data("AAPL", "price")["price"] != 0.0`

title: Two incompatible `ExtractionResult` dataclasses with same name in same package
description: `multi_source_extractor.py:46` defines `ExtractionResult` with `data: Optional[Dict]`; `unlimited_data_extractor.py:56` defines `ExtractionResult` with `data: Any`. `etl_orchestrator.py:23` imports from `multi_source_extractor`; `data_extractor.py:20` imports from `unlimited_extractor_with_fallbacks` which re-exports from `unlimited_data_extractor`. Code paths using different imports will type-mismatch silently.
recommendation: Consolidate into one canonical `ExtractionResult` in a new `backend/etl/types.py`; both extractors import from it.
acceptance_test_hint: `from backend.etl.types import ExtractionResult; from backend.etl.multi_source_extractor import ExtractionResult as R2; assert ExtractionResult is R2`

title: Placeholder contact email in SEC EDGAR User-Agent header
description: SEC EDGAR terms of service require a valid email contact in the User-Agent string for programmatic access. `contact@example.com` is a placeholder that violates SEC terms and can result in IP bans.
recommendation: Replace with a real operational email via environment variable: `os.getenv('SEC_EDGAR_CONTACT_EMAIL', '')`. Fail loudly at startup if empty.
acceptance_test_hint: `assert "example.com" not in client.headers["User-Agent"]`

title: `self.extractor` referenced in legacy methods but never assigned
description: `extract_phase()` at line 387 calls `await self.extractor.batch_extract(...)` and `run_realtime_update()` at line 633 calls `await self.extractor.extract_all_data(ticker)`. `ETLOrchestrator.__init__` assigns `self.legacy_extractor` but never `self.extractor`. Both methods will raise `AttributeError` at runtime.
recommendation: Rename `self.legacy_extractor` to `self.extractor` or add `self.extractor = self.legacy_extractor` in `__init__`.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_etl_modules.py -k "realtime"` passes

title: SQLite connections opened per-call with no context manager — connection leak on exception
description: All 8 `sqlite3.connect()` calls in `distributed_batch_processor.py` use bare `conn = sqlite3.connect(...)` / `conn.close()` pattern with no `with` statement or try/finally. If any exception occurs between open and close, the connection leaks. Under concurrent job processing this accumulates open file handles.
recommendation: Replace all with `with sqlite3.connect(self.job_db_path) as conn:` pattern, or use a single connection pool.
acceptance_test_hint: `lsof -p <pid> | grep job_tracking.db` shows no accumulation over 100 iterations

title: Kafka consumer uses auto-commit — no exactly-once guarantee for financial data
description: `enable_auto_commit: bool = True` in `KafkaConfig`. For financial event streams (stock prices, recommendations, audit_logs), auto-commit means offsets are committed before processing completes. A crash mid-processing loses events. Duplicate processing is also possible on consumer restart.
recommendation: Set `enable_auto_commit=False` and commit offsets manually after successful processing in the consumer loop. Consider `isolation_level="read_committed"` for transactional producers.
acceptance_test_hint: Integration test: kill consumer mid-batch, verify no duplicate or missing messages on restart

title: Airflow 1.x operator imports break DAG loading on Airflow 2.x
description: `from airflow.operators.python_operator import PythonOperator`, `from airflow.operators.bash_operator import BashOperator`, `from airflow.sensors.external_task_sensor import ExternalTaskSensor`, and `from airflow.utils.dates import days_ago` are removed in Airflow 2.x. The DAG will fail to parse, blocking all ML training.
recommendation: Replace with `from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator`, `from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator`, `from airflow.sensors.external_task import ExternalTaskSensor`, and `from airflow.utils.dates import days_ago` (or use `datetime.now() - timedelta(days=1)` directly).
acceptance_test_hint: `airflow dags list 2>&1 | grep ml_training_pipeline` shows no error; DAG appears in UI.

title: `np` used without importing numpy in `evaluate_models`
description: `evaluate_models` calls `np.random.randn(100)` at lines 510-511 but `numpy` is never imported at module level or inside the function. At runtime this raises `NameError: name 'np' is not defined`, crashing model evaluation and blocking deployment.
recommendation: Add `import numpy as np` at the top of `ml_training_pipeline_dag.py`. Also replace the placeholder `np.random.randn` calls with actual test-set predictions from the registry or remove the stub with a proper note.
acceptance_test_hint: Run `python -c "from data_pipelines.airflow.dags.ml_training_pipeline_dag import evaluate_models"` with no error; verify `import numpy as np` appears in file header.

title: `DataQualityChecker.check_recent_data_quality` does not exist
description: `check_data_quality` calls `checker.check_recent_data_quality(table="price_history", days_back=7)` but `DataQualityChecker` in `backend/utils/data_quality.py` exposes no such method (confirmed by reading all `def` lines 33-755). At runtime this raises `AttributeError`, causing the task to fail and — because `task_quality >> task_prepare` — blocking all downstream training.
recommendation: Either implement `check_recent_data_quality` in `DataQualityChecker` (querying `price_history` and checking `missing_data_rate`/`anomaly_rate`) or rewrite `check_data_quality` in the DAG to call the existing `generate_quality_report` method.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "def check_recent_data_quality" backend/utils/data_quality.py` returns a hit; DAG task `check_data_quality` completes with state `success` in a test run.

title: VACUUM ANALYZE inside implicit transaction fails at runtime
description: `cleanup_and_optimize` iterates `cleanup_queries` including `"VACUUM ANALYZE price_history"` and calls `pg_hook.run(query)`. `PostgresHook.run()` wraps each call in a transaction by default; PostgreSQL does not allow VACUUM inside a transaction block and raises `ProgrammingError: VACUUM cannot run inside a transaction block`.
recommendation: Run VACUUM statements separately with `autocommit=True` using a raw `psycopg2` connection: `conn = pg_hook.get_conn(); conn.set_isolation_level(0); conn.cursor().execute("VACUUM ANALYZE price_history"); conn.close()`.
acceptance_test_hint: `cleanup_and_optimize` task completes with state `success`; Airflow logs show `VACUUM ANALYZE price_history` executed without error.

title: `schedule_interval` deprecated in Airflow 2.4+; removed in 3.x
description: All three DAGs (`daily_stock_pipeline.py:122`, `enhanced_stock_pipeline.py:40`, `ml_training_pipeline_dag.py:125`) use `schedule_interval=`. This parameter was deprecated in Airflow 2.4 in favour of `schedule=` and will be removed in Airflow 3.x, causing DAG parse errors.
recommendation: Replace `schedule_interval='...'` with `schedule='...'` in all three DAGs.
acceptance_test_hint: `airflow dags list` shows all three DAGs with no `RemovedInAirflow3Warning`; grep for `schedule_interval` in all three files returns no hits.

title: `airflow.utils.db.create_session` removed in Airflow 2.x
description: `ensure_pool_exists()` (line 166) imports and uses `create_session` from `airflow.utils.db`. This internal API was removed in Airflow 2.3+. On modern Airflow versions the DAG file fails to parse.
recommendation: Replace with the public API: use `from airflow.models import Pool` and `from airflow.settings import Session` or create the pool via `airflow pools set stock_api_pool 8 "Stock API pool"` at deployment time and remove the runtime pool creation entirely.
acceptance_test_hint: `python -c "from data_pipelines.airflow.dags.daily_stock_pipeline import dag"` completes without `ImportError`; Airflow UI lists `daily_stock_pipeline`.

title: `parallel_fetch_stock_data` is dead code (superseded by dynamic task mapping)
description: The comment block at lines 1683-1694 explicitly marks `parallel_fetch_stock_data`, `calculate_indicators_parallel`, `process_stock_batch`, and `fetch_batch_data_worker` as deprecated. None are referenced in the DAG task graph. This dead code (~270 lines) adds confusion and maintenance burden, including a duplicated `calculate_rsi`/`calculate_macd` pair also explicitly labelled `DEPRECATED` (lines 777-821).
recommendation: Delete all functions marked `DEPRECATED` in the `# LEGACY FUNCTIONS` section and the `calculate_rsi`/`calculate_macd` stubs to reduce the file from ~1695 to ~1400 lines.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "DEPRECATED\ | Legacy" data_pipelines/airflow/dags/daily_stock_pipeline.py` returns no hits.

title: `evaluate_models` uses placeholder random data instead of real test predictions
description: Inside `_evaluate_models`, `monitor.calculate_metrics(y_true=np.random.randn(100), y_pred=np.random.randn(100), ...)` always produces meaningless metrics. The comment confirms this is a stub. This means the `best_model` selected for production deployment is chosen on random noise — not actual model quality.
recommendation: Load real held-out test labels and model predictions from the model registry or a dedicated test dataset stored at training time. At minimum gate deployment on `ranking_score > threshold`.
acceptance_test_hint: Model evaluation task logs show real metric values (e.g., non-zero R², finite MAE) derived from actual predictions; unit test uses fixture data instead of random arrays.

title: Placeholder alert email `ml-alerts@company.com` hardcoded in DAG
description: `default_args['email']` is set to `['ml-alerts@company.com']`. Airflow will attempt to deliver failure alerts to an external `company.com` address, which either silently drops (if not routed) or leaks pipeline failure details to an unintended domain.
recommendation: Replace with the actual alert address from an Airflow Variable or environment variable: `Variable.get("ML_ALERT_EMAIL", default_var="your-team@yourdomain.com")`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep "company.com" data_pipelines/airflow/dags/ml_training_pipeline_dag.py` returns no hits.

title: `analyze_sentiment` called with wrong signature
description: `_run_sentiment_analysis` calls `self.sentiment_engine.analyze_sentiment(ticker, text_data)` where `ticker` is a `str` and `text_data` is a `List[Dict]`. The method signature at `sentiment_analysis.py:130` is `analyze_sentiment(self, text: str, source: str = "unknown")` — it expects a single text string, not a ticker + list. Every real recommendation call fails with an `AttributeError` (`str object has no attribute 'get'`) when the engine tries to iterate the text.
recommendation: Replace with `await self.sentiment_engine.analyze_stock_sentiment(ticker, [item['text'] for item in text_data])` which is the correct batch method at `sentiment_analysis.py:238`.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/test_recommendation_engine.py -k test_run_sentiment` raises no exception and returns a `SentimentResult`

title: `scan_market_streaming` does not exist on `MarketScanner`
description: `OptimizedRecommendationEngine._scan_market_optimized` calls `scanner.scan_market_streaming(...)` as an async generator. `MarketScanner` only exposes `scan_market(...)` (non-streaming). Every call to `generate_daily_recommendations` on the optimized engine raises `AttributeError`.
recommendation: Implement `scan_market_streaming` on `MarketScanner` as an async generator that yields chunks, or fall back to `scan_market` inside a single-yield generator wrapper.
acceptance_test_hint: `await engine.generate_daily_recommendations(max_recommendations=5)` completes without `AttributeError`

title: `sensitivity_analysis` mutates `self.terminal_growth_rate`
description: Inside the nested loop `self.terminal_growth_rate = gr` permanently modifies the instance, so the final `gr` value persists after the method returns. Subsequent valuations use the last growth rate, not the configured default.
recommendation: Refactor to pass the growth rate as a parameter to `calculate_intrinsic_value` without touching `self`. E.g. use a local variable `orig = self.terminal_growth_rate` and restore it in a `finally` block, or — better — make `terminal_growth_rate` a parameter of the method.
acceptance_test_hint: `model.sensitivity_analysis(...)` followed by `model.terminal_growth_rate` equals initial value

title: `ranking_score` set on dataclass without declared field
description: `rank_recommendations` and `rank_recommendations_optimized` both assign `rec.ranking_score = ...` dynamically. `StockRecommendation` at `recommendation_types.py:32` is a `@dataclass` with no `ranking_score` field. Python allows dynamic attributes but `dataclasses.asdict` (called in `hybrid_engine.py:330`) silently drops undeclared fields, so the score is lost during serialisation. The sorted key also fails type checking.
recommendation: Add `ranking_score: float = field(default=0.0)` to `StockRecommendation` in `recommendation_types.py`.
acceptance_test_hint: `dataclasses.asdict(rec)` includes `ranking_score` key

title: `EnhancedStockRecommendation` references non-existent `overall_score` and `recommendation` fields
description: `_calculate_hybrid_score` accesses `self.overall_score` (line 50, 62) and `_create_error_recommendation` passes `overall_score=0.5, recommendation="HOLD"` (lines 427–428) as keyword arguments to a constructor of `EnhancedStockRecommendation` which inherits from `StockRecommendation`. Neither `overall_score` nor `recommendation` exist on the parent dataclass. This raises `TypeError` at instantiation in the error path.
recommendation: Remove the unsupported fields from `_create_error_recommendation`, replace `overall_score` references with `confidence` or a computed combination of sub-scores, or add the fields to the dataclass.
acceptance_test_hint: Error fallback path executes without `TypeError`

title: `get_news_sentiment` and `get_social_sentiment` are stubs
description: Both methods return hardcoded neutral scores with `sources_analyzed=0`, documented with "Placeholder implementation". `analyze_comprehensive_sentiment` compounds both stubs, always returning a 0.0-score result. This placeholder propagates into every recommendation that uses comprehensive sentiment.
recommendation: Implement real news and social data fetching or integrate with the data ingestion layer (`backend/data_ingestion/`). If not yet feasible, at minimum log a prominent warning and raise `NotImplementedError` so callers know the feature is inactive.
acceptance_test_hint: `analyze_comprehensive_sentiment("AAPL")` returns `sources_analyzed > 0`

title: Johansen test falls back to Engle-Granger silently
description: `_johansen_test` is documented as the Johansen cointegration test but simply delegates to `_engle_granger_test` with a comment "for full version use statsmodels". `CointegrationMethod.JOHANSEN` is a public enum member, creating a misleading contract.
recommendation: Either implement Johansen via `statsmodels.tsa.vector_ar.vecm.coint_johansen` or remove the `JOHANSEN` enum value and document the limitation explicitly.
acceptance_test_hint: Calling `test_cointegration(s1, s2, CointegrationMethod.JOHANSEN)` returns a different (or clearly-documented identical) result

title: Risk-free rate hardcoded at local scope during risk calculation
description: `risk_free_rate = 0.045` is declared as a local variable inside `_calculate_risk_metrics`. This makes updating the rate require a source edit and means the Sharpe ratio uses a different rate than `FundamentalAnalysisEngine.risk_free_rate`.
recommendation: Promote to a class attribute on `RecommendationEngine` and ensure it matches `FundamentalAnalysisEngine.risk_free_rate`, or inject via configuration.
acceptance_test_hint: Both engines reference the same configurable rate source

title: Portfolio size hardcoded at `$100,000`
description: `portfolio_size = 100_000` in `calculate_position_sizing` means all `max_position_size` values in `StockRecommendation` assume a fixed $100K portfolio, which is irrelevant to actual user portfolios.
recommendation: Accept `portfolio_size` as a parameter (default to $100,000 for backward compatibility) and thread it through from `RecommendationEngine`.
acceptance_test_hint: `max_position_size` scales correctly when portfolio_size=500_000

title: `PortfolioOptimizer.optimize` ignores `target_return` and `target_volatility`
description: The signature accepts `target_return` and `target_volatility` but the implementation ignores them and always returns equal-weight allocation. The `get_efficient_frontier` method calls `optimize` in a loop across different target returns, but all calls produce identical equal-weight results, generating a degenerate flat "frontier".
recommendation: Implement mean-variance optimisation (via `scipy.optimize` or `cvxpy`) that respects the target constraints, or replace with the existing `backend/utils/portfolio_optimizer.py` which has a proper async solver.
acceptance_test_hint: Efficient frontier has monotonically increasing volatility with return
